t: Ebla, at Tell Mardikh near Aleppo, was the capital of a Bronze Age kingdom in northern Syria.
Its palace archive of about 17,000 tablets and fragments records a Semitic-speaking state of the 24th century BCE.
Destroyed around 2300 and again around 2000 BCE, it revived under Amorite kings until the Hittites destroyed it c. 1600 BCE.
dyk: The fire that destroyed Ebla’s palace around 2300 BCE baked its clay tablets hard, preserving one of the largest archives of the third millennium BCE.
ev: Mari’s kings press Ebla, which pays large amounts of silver and gold
Ebla, allied with Nagar and Kish, defeats Mari
Palace G burns, probably at the hands of Akkad or Mari
The second Ebla is destroyed; Amorites later rebuild the city
Ebla becomes a vassal of Yamhad, centred on Aleppo
A statue of King Ibbit-Lim identifies Tell Mardikh as Ebla
Italian excavators find the Palace G archive
